column1: #   args     '-' for none, otherwise an argument list split on spaces
#   shape    an extended regular expression EVERY line of stdout must match,
#            with \t standing for a tab; '-' means stdout must be EMPTY
#   rc       the exit status the contract promises
# The names %JAIL% %VM% %HELD% %ABSENT% %BADNAME% are filled in by
# tests/conformance/run.subr from the world of the adapter under test; see its
# header. Nothing here may be destructive: these vectors run against a real
# node in tier 5. The mutating verbs appear only with a name their contract
# requires them to refuse before they touch anything.
# Field order comes from the '# contract:' line above each function in
# every adapter states the same one.
# An ABSOLUTE PATH is all the shared contract says (the '# contract:' line
# reads "-> path"). It used to read ^/.+/%JAIL%$ here, which is CBSD's layout
# -- ${jailsysdir}/<name> -- written into an oracle three adapters answer:
# a pseudo-cluster guest keeps its configuration in a dataset CHILD, at
# <mount>/<name>/sys, precisely so that it travels with the guest (D-84 item 3),
# and it failed this row the first time the suite was pointed at it (tier 5).
# The layout each platform actually promises is pinned per adapter, harder than
# a suffix match was: tests/tier5/t_conformance_real.sh asserts the exact
# ${jailsysdir}/<name> AND that rc.conf_<name> is in it, and
# adapter_guest_links for a guest that is WHERE THIS PLATFORM KEEPS IT needs
# nothing reconciled, on every platform -- which is what %DATAPATH% names. It
# used to read "%JAIL% jail" with a made-up path and the claim that a jail is
# empty everywhere; tier 5 showed that to be a claim about CBSD and not about
# every adapter. The pseudo-cluster's fixed sysdir path means a guest whose
# data is somewhere else DOES need one link there, for either type, which is
# what lets a guest promoted onto a path its home node chose be found at all.
# So the shared row says the thing that is true of all three, and each
# platform's own answer for a guest that is NOT at that path is pinned where
# the platform is real -- t_conformance_real.sh for CBSD (a jail needs none
# wherever its data is), t_conformance_pseudo.sh for the pseudo-cluster (one
# link, named), tests/tier4/t_adapter_parse.sh for the real adapter's VM.
# The same treatment adapter_guest_sysdir already gets, above, and for the
# The data path is an ARGUMENT now (D-181) and every adapter checks it: a
# caller that has not read the guest's configuration has nothing to pass, and a
# relative one is a link into whatever directory the promotion ran in.
# Where the PLATFORM says a guest's data is (D-178): read, never derived, and
# the ceremony's post-registration check is against this answer.
# Where the GUEST'S OWN CONFIGURATION says its data is, read before anything is
# mounted (D-181). Three files, in each adapter's own spelling of a guest
# configuration, provided by the test file that runs these vectors: one that
# names an absolute path, one that names none, one that names something a
# replica cannot be mounted at. The three answers are three different verdicts
# and no adapter may blur them -- a fallback where the real answer is "refuse"
# is a replica mounted somewhere nobody meant.
